questions.question: You hear a siren while driving but cannot see the emergency vehicle yet. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
Slow down. Don't stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren but don't know where the emergency vehicle is, pull safely to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you know it is not coming toward you.

questions.question: What should drivers do when driving in bad weather?

options.text: Speed up to reach their destination faster.
Follow the vehicle ahead more closely.
Stay farther away from the vehicle ahead.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: When driving on wet roads, increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead of you.

questions.question: Two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different roads. Which vehicle must yield?

options.text: Either one
The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
Neither

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule applies at intersections with signs, signals, or no traffic control.

questions.question: An approaching driver is not dimming their high beam headlights. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the oncoming vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight ahead down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you see the road well enough to stay on course until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone
Wrong way
Railroad crossing
Stop

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs are only used to show a no passing zone.

questions.question: How much alcohol does your body get rid of per hour?

options.text: Three drinks an hour
One drink an hour
Two drinks an hour
None of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: One drink an hour
questions.explanation: The average person's body processes about one drink per hour. How impaired someone becomes depends on many factors: how much they drank, how fast they drank it, their weight, how much they have eaten, and their health.

questions.question: What does a single broken yellow line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and drivers can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction and drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions and drivers can pass when safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Dashed lines mean drivers next to the line can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What is the legal blood alcohol limit for drivers 21 and older?

options.text: 0.05 percent
0.08 percent
0.02 percent
0.1 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: For drivers 21 and older, driving with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.08 percent or higher is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: You have a green light and want to turn left, but oncoming traffic is heavy. What should you do?

options.text: Use the next intersection.
Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Turn because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: You can enter the intersection on green to prepare for your left turn. Wait in the center until oncoming traffic passes before turning.

questions.question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, what should you do?

options.text: Depend on road signs to find your way.
Plan your trip in advance.
Only need to know roughly where you are going.
Always choose the most direct route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip in advance.
questions.explanation: Plan your trip before you start driving. Check your destination on a map before you leave. Don't start with only a vague idea of where you are going.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
Keep your front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb when parking uphill. This keeps your car from rolling into traffic if it moves. If there is no curb, turn the wheels sharply toward the edge of the road.

questions.question: If a green arrow becomes a solid green light, what can you do?

options.text: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
You may no longer turn and must go straight.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You no longer have to turn in the direction the arrow pointed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you may still turn in that direction. However, you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What is a "No zone"?

options.text: A designated no passing zone
A one-way traffic area
The blind spot of a large vehicle
An area designated for motor vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spot of a large vehicle
questions.explanation: "No zones" are the large blind spots around trucks and big vehicles. Drivers of smaller vehicles should not stay in these areas.

questions.question: Which statement about motorcycles is true?

options.text: It is okay for drivers to follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two people is more balanced than one with just the rider.
You must completely change lanes when passing a motorcycle.
Motorcycle brake lights always turn on when the rider slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must completely change lanes when passing a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use a full lane. Make sure your entire vehicle is in the left lane before passing a motorcycle.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Start up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When a driver extends their left arm downward, they are signaling that they will stop. If you are following this driver, adjust your speed accordingly.

questions.question: When should you allow more space between your vehicle and the one in front?

options.text: On an uphill slope.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: On an uphill slope.
questions.explanation: Allow extra space in front of your vehicle when stopped on an uphill slope. This gives you room if the vehicle in front rolls backward when traffic starts moving.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no warning lights or gates, what should you do?

options.text: Cross the tracks quickly as fast as you can.
Always stop before crossing.
Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to beat any oncoming train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to trains before crossing railroad tracks, especially if there are no lights or gates. Do not cross until your entire vehicle can fit on the other side. Do not shift gears while crossing because your vehicle might stall.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway slants left. What does this mean?

options.text: There is an intersection just ahead.
You are approaching a construction area.
You will need to turn left just ahead.
The road will get narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will get narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line on the side of the road marks the edge of the travel lane. When this line angles toward the center of the road, it means the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and you cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and you can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and you cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction and you can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and you cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Narrow bridge ahead.
A lane ends or the road narrows ahead.
Industrial area.
Freeway on-ramp ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lane ends or the road narrows ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign warns you that a lane is ending or the road is narrowing.

questions.question: If you are convicted of driving while intoxicated a second time within five years, what will happen?

options.text: You will lose your license for only 90 days.
You will be limited to driving on residential roads only.
You will be required to install an Ignition Interlock Device (IID).
You will be required to drive 10 mph under the speed limit at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be required to install an Ignition Interlock Device (IID).
questions.explanation: A second DWI conviction within five years has serious consequences. Your license may be suspended for one year, denied for five years, or both. You may face a $1,000 fine and up to one year in jail. Most importantly, you must install an Ignition Interlock Device before you can get your license back.

questions.question: How far could a fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph need to come to a complete stop?

options.text: 50 feet
125 feet
400 feet
750 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 400 feet
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks stop much slower than cars at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer needs almost 400 feet to stop when driving at 55 mph.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Blow your horn, steer right, and speed up.
Blow your horn, steer left, and brake.
Blow your horn, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, blow your horn, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blow your horn, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: First, blow your horn to get the other driver's attention. If they do not move, steer to the right to escape. Do not steer left because if the other driver swerves at the last moment, you will still crash. Brake firmly and steadily. Slowing down even a few miles per hour will reduce the impact.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow arrow at a traffic signal?

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction of the arrow.
Come to a complete stop.
You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way and oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in that direction. However, oncoming traffic has a green light, so you must yield to them and to any pedestrians before turning.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to the lane you just left.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the lane you just left.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane closest to where you came from. This keeps you safe and follows traffic rules.
